name: Final Inspection
tagline: Friday. Week four. The clipboard cometh.
notes: Plays when the player goes to bed on the last week. The house passes only if all four maladies are fixed (housefixed, i.e. fixedcount == storycount); the game uses the same rule to decide whether the finale podcast plays. On a fail, Dan walks to each room that is still broken (kitchen, bedroom closet, bathroom, living room, in that order) via single conditional choices, so the scene names exactly what's unfinished.

lines: *Friday morning. Inspector Dan arrives with his clipboard, his windbreaker and, for once, completely dry shoes.*
Dan: Final inspection. Let's see what we've got.
*The kitchen. He checks every pipe, knocks on the walls and peers under the sink for a long time.*
Dan: Not a single leak. You've really turned the tide on this place.
*The bedroom closet. Bare studs, fresh drywall, no smell at all. He sniffs anyway.*
Dan: No more fungus among us. I'll be honest, I'll miss the moldy oldie. Spore-adically.
*The living room. He flips every switch in the house. Nothing flickers. Nothing sparks. Nothing apologizes.*
Dan: Rewired, up to code. A real watt-ershed moment.
*The bathroom. He runs a thumb along the grout of the old pink tile and smiles.*
Dan: Restored, regrouted, sealed. I said it on Monday and I'll tile it again: she's a keeper.
*He waits for a laugh. The whole house holds its breath, very politely.*
Dan: Congratulations. 12 Heartbreak Lane passes. Every room. I'll tell the council it's the safest house on the street.
*Friday morning. Inspector Dan arrives with his clipboard. He isn't smiling.*
Dan: Final inspection. Every room, top to bottom. I promised the council.

choices.text: Follow him to the living room.

lines: *He goes straight to the kitchen sink.*
*Drip. Drip. Drip.*
Dan: Ah. That's an active leak. In the house I promised would be bone dry.
*Behind him, the tap drips once more. It sounds almost apologetic.*

choices.text: Follow him to the living room.

lines: *He opens the bedroom closet. The back wall is velvet black, and it seems to be sulking.*
Dan: Black mold. Still here. A fungus among us. ...It's less funny the second time.
*Something in the closet sighs, at length.*

choices.text: Follow him to the living room.

lines: *He taps the pink tile by the tub. It's still cracked. Water's been getting in behind it, and two tiles come away in his hand.*
Dan: Loose, cracked, and the wall behind it's soft. I wanted to call it a keeper. I can't keep it like this.
*He puts the tiles back very gently, like he's apologizing to them.*

choices.text: Follow him to the living room.

lines: *He flips the living-room switch. The lamp flickers, nervously. Somewhere in the wall, something sparks and then goes very quiet.*
Dan: That's a fire waiting for a cold night. I don't have a pun for that one. I looked.
*Dan stands in the hall and writes for a long time.*
Dan: I'm sorry. I really am. It's so close. But I can only sign off a house that's fixed for real, every room of it.
Dan: I'll have to recommend the demolition goes ahead.
